A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H. Corresponding content can be matched despite reformatting and the added NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: v2 reports original microstructure generation, metamaterial inverse-design, and copyright-constrained generation experiments, with additional results in Appendix E.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and their numerical and visual results, including the appendix evaluations.

M1.justification: The latent correction procedure, Algorithms 1–2, surrogate constraints, and simulator-based optimization are retained. Section 5 makes the previously described perturbation-based gradient estimation more explicit without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same microstructure data, mechanical metamaterials, and Mickey Mouse/Jerry image dataset. The appendix interpolation and extrapolation scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: Cond, PDM, and Bastek and Kochmann remain in their corresponding comparisons. Appendix E retains Image Space Correction and Learned Latent Corrector. Listing Bastek and Kochmann upfront in v4 does not add a comparator; v2 already evaluates it in Section 6.2.

E3.justification: The image preprocessing and resolutions, 8,000-image cartoon dataset, M=10 simulator perturbations, five-step DPO comparison, and evaluation metrics are retained. No changed experimental protocol is reported.

E4.justification: The void-diameter analysis, successive DPO corrections, interpolation/extrapolation examples, copyright denoising trajectories, and failed alternative-correction analyses remain. No new ablation or robustness analysis is introduced.

E5.justification: The existing uncertainty values and reporting practice are retained. The new checklist states that error bars are included, but adds no run counts, seeds, uncertainty definitions, or statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Main and appendix results match, including the proposed method's microstructure FID of 13.5±3.1, metamaterial MSE of 1.4±0.6, and copyright constraint satisfaction of 90% with FID 65.1. Appendix examples, qualitative findings, and Table 1 runtimes are retained.

T1.justification: Section 5 adds an explicit expectation defining Gaussian smoothing and a gradient identity for the smoothed simulator, extending the earlier Monte Carlo explanation. The feasibility and fidelity theorems, assumptions, and proofs in Appendices G–H remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims about training-free proximal constraint enforcement, feasibility and fidelity guarantees, and applicability across the three demonstrated domains are retained in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion.

C2.justification: The interpretations of constraint satisfaction versus fidelity, simulator accuracy and computational cost, and surrogate accuracy limits are retained. Appendix A preserves the same limitations and proposed extensions to video generation and external simulators.

D1.justification: v4 newly provides a repository link and states that all code has been released. Section 5 also specifies Gaussian perturbations and absorption of the gradient estimator's scaling factor into the step size. Existing hardware, runtimes, and implementation settings are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds Dontas et al.'s work on text-to-image latent diffusion for blind inverse problems. The introduction more explicitly distinguishes training-time distribution-level adherence from inference-time enforcement. The extensive related-work discussion in Appendix B is otherwise retained.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites of the introduction, projection explanation, simulator-gradient discussion, and baseline list. v4 adds a NeurIPS checklist, reorders the credits sections, and renames Appendix H, while retaining the main scientific narrative and appendix organization.

P2.justification: The NeurIPS format changes front matter, typography, margins, and float placement. Retained figures are rescaled; Figures 4 and 8 add an increasing-strain label, and Figures 4–5 have revised captions. No scientific figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: The explicit simulator-gradient formulation, clearer baseline organization, and new code-access pointer modestly improve explanation and reproducibility documentation. The added strain labels also clarify the figures. The experimental evidence and convergence proofs remain essentially unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
